title: Along Florida’s Gulf Coast, Residents Breathe Easier After Hurricane Isaias Passes
partialText: Beachside towns normally teeming with tourists were hit by fallen trees and power outages, not catastrophic flooding.

title: Were Isaias Forecasts Accurate?
partialText: Many people in the storm’s path escaped the worst, but 4 people were killed and there was plenty of damage.

title: Rebuking Ukraine Over Oil Strikes, Trump Says It Should ‘Get a New President’
partialText: Hours after President Trump said the United States would buy Russian diesel, the Kremlin said there would be no immediate resumption of discussions to end the war.

title: Economic Pain and an Unpopular Trump Put G.O.P. on its Heels With Three Weeks to Go
partialText: Inflation has hurt Americans at many levels: Farmers, truckers, consumers. It has also expanded the electoral map into what was safely Republican country just a few months ago.

title: Fact-Checking Senate Ads in Iowa, New Hampshire and North Carolina
partialText: We assess three campaign ads in the battleground states that have focused on the cost of living.

title: Christa Pike Discharged From Hospital After Surviving Execution Attempt
partialText: Ms. Pike, 50 and convicted of the 1995 murder of a classmate, survived two doses of the drug pentobarbital late last month.

title: Fort Hood Shooter’s Execution Could Face Challenge in Federal Courts
partialText: Legal experts say the former Army officer convicted in a 2009 mass shooting could face a narrow, rushed path to appeal a public execution by firing squad.

title: Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh Airport Attacked Again, After Days of Houthi Strikes
partialText: Flights were diverted from the airport in the capital of Saudi Arabia, which has faced repeated deadly attacks from the Iran-backed militia in Yemen.

title: How Cornell University Chi Phi Fraternity Members Responded After Rape Accusation
partialText: Records reveal how fraternity members responded when a fellow student accused them of sexual assault.

title: At Cornell, a Sorority Finds Itself Sued by One of Its Own
partialText: Some Delta Delta Delta members are asking if the sorority shares blame in the bombshell case — or if the group is a scapegoat.

title: She’s Been to Gaza. She Met With the Iranians. Now She Has a Warning.
partialText: As the head of the International Committee of the Red Cross, Mirjana Spoljaric goes to both sides of conflicts. She’s worried that our warring world is spiraling out of control.

title: How Is Child Marriage Still Legal in the U.S.?
partialText: Children are still allowed to marry here in the United States because of zealots on the left and right alike.

title: We Had Questions About A.I. Joseph Gordon-Levitt Had Answers.
partialText: The actor takes Times Opinion to the United Nations to explore what’s at stake with A.I.

title: Indian Police Round Up Protest Leaders and Lock Down Delhi
partialText: Thousands of young people tried to gather to protest a sweeping revision of their country’s voter roll. Security forces hauled many of them away.
